questions.prompt: Covariance eigenvalues of centred data are 9, 3, 1, 1. What fraction of variance do the first two components explain? (decimal, tolerance 0.001)
With the eigenvalues 9, 3, 1, 1, what is the mean squared reconstruction error if you keep 2 components? (decimal, tolerance 0.001)
In power iteration, what does the update v ← Cv/‖Cv‖ converge to (for a generic start)?
options: The eigenvector of C belonging to the largest eigenvalue of C
The eigenvector of C belonging to the smallest eigenvalue of C
The mean of the data, because C is built from the centred points
A random unit vector, because the start is random and generic
questions.explanation: Components along larger eigenvalues are amplified faster, so the direction converges to the top eigenvector.
Dot product is 0, so the vectors are orthogonal.

questions.prompt: u=(1,1) and v=(5,5) differ in length. What is their cosine similarity, and what is their Euclidean distance? Give the Euclidean distance. (decimal, tolerance 0.01)
questions.explanation: Cosine is 1 (same direction), but the distance is sqrt(32)=5.66: cosine ignores scale.

questions.prompt: An embedding table for 8,000 sensor-place IDs uses 64 dimensions. How many parameters? (integer, tolerance 1)
Why is an embedding layer implemented as a table lookup rather than multiplying a one-hot vector by a matrix?
options: One-hot vectors cannot be multiplied by a matrix, so the product is undefined
Lookups make the embedding non-trainable, which keeps the table stable
Both give the same row, but indexing avoids V multiplications and a V-length vector
The lookup gives a different and better result than the one-hot product does
questions.explanation: E^T e_i = E_i; the lookup just reads the row.

questions.prompt: Classes differ along axis x (std 0.3 within class) while an irrelevant axis y has std 3. After PCA with k=1, what happens?
options: PCA automatically uses the labels to choose x as the retained axis
Both axes are kept, because the class axis has a small variance
The retained feature is the nuisance axis y and the class information is lost
The retained feature is the class axis x, because it separates the classes
questions.explanation: PCA ranks by variance only: var(y)=9 exceeds var(x)≈1.

questions.prompt: Which protocol is leakage-free for 'frozen features vs raw inputs'?
options: Fit the encoder on train+test features, because that makes it more stable
Select k on the test accuracy and then report that same accuracy
Compare the two kinds of features on one labelled set only, with no held-out set
Fit the encoder on a pool without the test set, train the head, and test once
questions.explanation: Anything fitted or selected on test data contaminates the estimate.

questions.prompt: Feature accuracy over 20 label draws: mean 0.84; raw baseline mean 0.78, draw-to-draw std of the gain 0.05. How many standard errors is the mean gain from zero? (decimal, tolerance 0.05; SE = std/√20)
You train a linear probe on a pretrained encoder with 200 labelled robot images and get 85% test accuracy. List the controls you need before claiming the encoder's features are good.
rubric: Raw-pixel (or simple handcrafted) baseline with the same head, labels and test set.
Several label draws/seeds with spread, and the encoder not trained on the test images.
A sanity check such as a random-weights encoder or shuffled labels, and a statement of what would falsify the claim.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

Check on a toy covariance with known eigenvalues (e.g. 4 and 1).
